working_title: County Down's Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Royal County Down, Ardglass and Kirkistown Castle
angle: County Down is already on every serious golfer's bucket list thanks to Royal County Down, but most visitors miss the two other links courses that complete a genuinely outstanding three-round circuit. This guide treats the county as a self-contained golf destination for UK visitors, covering the practicalities of visitor access and green fees alongside the less-discussed supporting cast.
research_notes:
- Royal County Down (Newcastle, Co. Down): founded 1889, designed originally by Old Tom Morris, later refined by Harry Colt and others. Championship Course par 71, 7,186 yards. Also has the shorter Annesley Links (par 66, 4,548 yards). Consistently ranked in the world's top five; ranked #1 by Golf Digest on its World's 100 Greatest Courses list for 2024.
- RCD Championship green fees (2026): £450 peak season (up from £425 in 2025, itself an 18% rise on 2024). Visitor tee times on Mon, Tue, Thu mornings, Fri and Sun afternoons only — advance booking essential. Annesley Links cheaper and more accessible.
- Ardglass Golf Club (Ardglass village, ~30 miles south of Belfast): par 70, 6,268 yards links. Clubhouse based in Ardglass Castle, parts of which date to 1405 — widely claimed as the oldest clubhouse in the world. Front five holes hug the Irish Sea coast. Notable halfway cottage at the back of the 7th green. Peak-season visitor green fees risen to around £220 for 2025 (per National Club Golfer report). Visitors welcome every day; handicap certificate required; limited practice facilities noted by reviewers.
- Kirkistown Castle Golf Club (Cloughey, Ards Peninsula): founded 1902, layout updated by James Braid in 1934. Par 70, ~6,167–6,283 yards depending on tees. Most easterly 18-hole course on the island of Ireland; nearest links to Belfast (~45 min by road). Visitors welcome every day, advance booking essential. Green fees notably lower than RCD or Ardglass — positioned as best-value links in Ulster. Highly rated for friendliness and value on GolfPass (4.6/5, 93% recommend).
- Getting there: Belfast City Airport (BHD) ~30–40 min by car to Bangor/Downpatrick/Newcastle. Belfast International (BFS) ~1 hr to County Down destinations. Ferries to Belfast from Cairnryan (Scotland, Stena Line and P&O Irish Sea) and Liverpool (Stena Line) — car ferry a practical option for UK golfers taking their own clubs. Newcastle is ~45 min from Belfast city via the A24.
- The three courses form a natural circuit: Kirkistown Castle on the Ards Peninsula (north-east Down), Ardglass on the south-east coast, Royal County Down at Newcastle on the south-west Mournes coast. Could be played over three days with Newcastle/Slieve Donard area as a base.
- Slieve Donard Resort & Spa sits adjacent to Royal County Down in Newcastle — frequently cited as the golfer's base for RCD. Burrendale Hotel also in Newcastle as a less expensive option.
- Clandeboye Golf Club (Dufferin Course, Newtownards) mentioned as a strong heathland/parkland alternative if adding a fourth day: par 71, 6,742 yards championship, elevated with sea views and gorse-lined fairways.
- Mourne Mountains provide dramatic backdrop for RCD; on clear days the Isle of Man visible from Ardglass.
- Visitor access note: RCD Championship Course is restricted to designated visitor days only — this is a key practical point for UK golfers used to more open access. Societies and packages available as an alternative route to securing times.
